s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on Magnetic Resonance Imaging
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The patient sustained a twisting injury to the affected hand while participating in acroyoga 2 years prior
The bruise and pain initially appeared a few days after the injury
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

raw.rationale: The presence of a painful bruise that persisted despite icing and resting, along with the pathology showing mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition and lesional cells that are spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, strongly supports the diagnosis of a Nora lesion, which is a rare, benign, and painful lesion of the subcutaneous tissue.

rejected.label: Fat necrosis
rejected.why: While fat necrosis can occur after trauma, the specific pathological features and immunohistochemistry results do not align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Subcutaneous pseudotumor
rejected.why: This term is more general and does not specifically match the detailed pathological findings described in the case.

rejected.label: Hematoma
rejected.why: The chronic nature of the lesion and the specific pathological features do not support a simple hematoma, which would typically resolve more quickly and not show the same level of tissue organization and cellular characteristics.

rejected.label: Sclerosing lipogranuloma
rejected.why: This condition typically involves a different set of pathological findings, including a prominent granulomatous reaction, which is not described in the case.
